title: Famous Inventions
description: Who invented what, and when: the breakthroughs that shaped modern life

questions.question: Who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received the US patent for the telephone in 1876, though others, such as Antonio Meucci and Elisha Gray, worked on similar devices.

questions.question: Which brothers made the first powered, controlled airplane flight in 1903?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903. The Montgolfiers pioneered hot-air balloons.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish. Florey and Chain later developed penicillin into a usable drug.

questions.question: Who proposed the World Wide Web in 1989?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the Web at CERN in 1989. Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP, the internet protocols the Web runs on.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization is credited with inventing paper around the 2nd century AD?
questions.explanation: Cai Lun of the Han dynasty is traditionally credited with papermaking around 105 AD. Egyptian papyrus was an earlier, different material.

questions.question: Who developed a successful smallpox vaccine in 1796?
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner used cowpox to protect against smallpox. Jonas Salk developed a polio vaccine in the 1950s.

questions.question: Whose improvements to the steam engine in the 1760s and 1770s helped drive the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: James Watt's separate condenser made steam engines much more efficient. Stephenson later built famous steam locomotives.

questions.question: Who is famous for developing a long-lasting incandescent light bulb in 1879?
questions.explanation: Thomas Edison's team produced a practical carbon-filament bulb in 1879. Joseph Swan developed a similar bulb in England around the same time.

questions.question: What did Karl Benz build in 1885-1886 that is often called the first practical automobile?
questions.explanation: The three-wheeled Benz Patent-Motorwagen ran on a gasoline engine. Ford's Model T arrived in 1908 and made cars affordable.

questions.question: What did Tim Berners-Lee, Johannes Gutenberg and Alexander Graham Bell all transform?
questions.explanation: The Web, the printing press and the telephone each changed how people share information over distance.
